doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: Closing remarks and a story about a birthday gift for his wife
summary: Rowe wraps up as film runs out; Appleyard chats about his wife's birthday DVD.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Man, you’ve got a million stories. And I wish we could keep going. We’re about to run out of film here. I enjoyed it so much and I’m looking forward to hearing you play tomorrow night.
Oh thanks. Great pleasure to be here.
And wish your wife a happy birthday for me.

Oh thanks, that’s nice of you. I took her out for dinner, and we had a lovely dinner and we saw four Italian singers, young boys, about a year ago, on the network that doesn’t have commercials, what’s that called?

And they were great, they really were. And I really liked them too. They sang a lot of the old Italian songs but their harmony was beautiful. Presentation was marvelous. So we sent away, I did, for the video. It was a hundred bucks. It was the kind of thing you join the club and pay a hundred bucks or whatever it was. And he never came. So she got on the phone, it was a DVD, got on the phone, and, “oh yes but we had a mix-up” and went on and went on. Anyway, it arrived about two months ago, and I didn’t say anything about it. So she keeps saying to me, “when are you going to give me the numbers on your credit card?” So anyway I had it as a surprise gift. Plus I gave her some American funds that I had. Because she’s got a daughter that works for one of the major stores in America as an accountant. She’s very good. And they’ve just moved her to Dallas. So I said, “here’s some Dallas money for you.”
Good. Well thanks so much for your time.
Well thank you. Lovely being here. Thanks for inviting me to play. © Fillius Jazz Archive -25-
